institution: Royal Conservatoire The Hague (Koninklijk Conservatorium) — Institute of Sonology
accreditationStatus: NVAO-accredited (Master of Music, University of the Arts The Hague / Hogeschool der Kunsten Den Haag)
language: English — 'The studies will be conducted in English and applicants are expected to be adequately fluent with the language.'
durationEcts: 2 years full-time; 120 ECTS (Dutch Master of Music standard; ECTS not stated on programme page — UNVERIFIED for exact credit total)
whatYouStudy: Electroacoustic music, computer music and sound art. Instruction in composition, live electronic music, field recording, sound installations, algorithmic composition, wave field synthesis, digital sound synthesis, analogue studio techniques, psychoacoustics, spatialisation. Independent research project plus thesis. 'Technology is not merely an adjunct to the existing music practice, but should be used primarily to explore new forms of composition.'
entryRequirements: 'The candidate should have a bachelor's diploma relevant for the professional field of Sonology (composition of electronic and/or acoustic music using fixed media, notation, improvisation or some combination of these, sound synthesis research, sound art, related subjects such as artificial intelligence, computer science or electronic engineering, musicology, music perception, film studies, or as a performing musician).' Plus a two-page study plan: (1) brief description of the proposed master's project (practical and/or theoretical), (2) time planning divided over four semesters, (3) detailed project description with central research question and context, (4) overview of subjects for the final thesis presentation.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly. The eligible bachelor list names 'artificial intelligence, computer science or electronic engineering' as relevant fields. A BSc Software Engineering falls squarely inside the stated list. This is one of the very few Field-A masters in Europe that names computer science as a qualifying bachelor.
portfolioSpec: 'Students for the Master of Music in Sonology are selected on the basis of a portfolio with previous compositions, sound installations, recordings of live performances or research results in the form of computer programs, articles, theses, etc.' No number of works, maximum duration or file format is stipulated on the official page — UNVERIFIED (open-ended portfolio).
auditionSpec: 'There is no live admission exam.' Selection is on portfolio + two-page study plan only.
tuitionNonEU: €11,488 per year (institutional tuition fee, Master's programmes, 2026-2027). EEA statutory fee is €2,694. Fees indexed annually.
otherFees: €24 administration fee if paying in 8 instalments. No application or audition fee mentioned.
totalCostEstimate: ≈ €22,976 tuition over 2 years + living costs The Hague (IND requires ~€1,100+/month proof of means) ≈ €26,000–29,000/yr total; ~€52,000–58,000 for the full degree — UNVERIFIED on living-cost figure.
scholarshipName: NL Scholarship (formerly Holland Scholarship); Excellence Scholarship
scholarships: NL Scholarship: €5,000, one-off, first year only, for non-EEA students. 'It is not possible to apply directly for an NL Scholarship; you will be informed if you have been nominated based on the results of your entrance exam and Master Plan.' Excellence Scholarship: for Master's candidates who perform best in the entrance exams, EEA and non-EEA eligible; amount UNVERIFIED. The two are mutually exclusive. Neither covers full tuition.
englishTest: IELTS minimum 6.0, or TOEFL minimum 80, or TOEIC, or Cambridge English. Non-EU/EEA students must submit proof before 1 September of the entry year.
deadline: 26 February (PRIOR-CYCLE REFERENCE: the 2026 intake deadline was 26 February 2026). For September 2027 entry expect a deadline around late February 2027 — UNVERIFIED, not yet published.
applicationOpens: Applications open after 1 December of the preceding year (for 2026 entry: after 1 December 2025).

institution: Royal Conservatoire The Hague — Institute of Sonology
qualification: NOT A DEGREE — course certificate only. 'The one-year Sonology course is not a degree programme and students are therefore not entitled to Dutch student finance or a student travel product.'
accreditationStatus: Not an NVAO-accredited degree programme (non-degree course at an NVAO-accredited institution)
language: English — 'All lessons are taught in English.'
durationEcts: 1 year (September to June); ECTS not awarded as a degree — UNVERIFIED
whatYouStudy: Digital sound synthesis, analogue studio techniques, free improvised music, algorithmic composition, psychoacoustics, sound installations, field recording and the spatialisation of sound.
entryRequirements: 'Admission to the course is determined on the basis of a portfolio and a motivation letter.' No bachelor's degree formally required.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — no degree prerequisite stated; admission is on portfolio and motivation letter alone. This is the standard route for people without conservatoire training, and many alumni progress into the Sonology Master afterwards.
portfolioSpec: Portfolio + motivation letter. Exact number/length/format not stipulated — UNVERIFIED.
tuitionNonEU: €2,590 for 2025–2026 (course fee, same for all nationalities; cannot be paid in instalments). Fee for 2026–2027 'will be announced in due time' — UNVERIFIED for 2027-28.
totalCostEstimate: ≈ €2,600 course fee + ~€13,000 living costs = ~€15,600 for the year — UNVERIFIED on living costs.
scholarships: No scholarship scheme identified for the One-Year Course; because it is not a degree programme it is generally excluded from the NL Scholarship and from Dutch student finance. UNVERIFIED whether an IND study residence permit can be issued for a non-degree course — this is a critical check for a Tunisian national and must be confirmed with the Royal Conservatoire before relying on this route.
englishTest: UNVERIFIED (no specific test score published for the One-Year Course)
deadline: 26 February (PRIOR CYCLE: 26 February 2026 for the September 2026 start). Expect late February 2027 for a September 2027 start — UNVERIFIED.
applicationOpens: After 1 December of the preceding year

program: Master Art of Sound (music recording, production and sound reinforcement)
qualification: Master of Music (MMus), Art of Sound
accreditationStatus: NVAO-accredited (University of the Arts The Hague)
durationEcts: 2 years; 120 ECTS — UNVERIFIED on exact ECTS
whatYouStudy: Recording, music production and sound reinforcement at professional level, built around a self-defined Master Project in which 'your artistic development, research and entrepreneurship play an important role'.
entryRequirements: Submit by the deadline: a Portfolio, a Master Project Plan, a Curriculum Vitae (Europass CV format) and a Motivation Form. 'Before you start the Art of Sound Master's study you must submit a Master Project Plan, in which you indicate your plans for the organization of your Master's study and your Master Project.'
acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED — the entry-requirements page states no specific bachelor field requirement, but the portfolio demands three self-designed professional recording/production/sound-reinforcement projects, which in practice requires substantial prior studio experience. For a candidate with no professional audio experience this is effectively a hard barrier.
portfolioSpec: EXACTLY: three (3) recording projects, music productions or sound reinforcement projects that you have designed yourself. For each project: media in 'lossless or uncompressed audio, possibly video' uploaded to file storage, PLUS a written report in PDF of 'minimum 300 words per project, maximum 600 words per project' covering project description, your tasks/responsibilities, creative vision, technological vision and evaluation of the result.
auditionSpec: Motivation interview, online via Microsoft Teams, 'max. 30 minutes per candidate', with three jury members, held only if portfolio and Master Project Plan are approved.
totalCostEstimate: ≈ €22,976 tuition + living ≈ €52,000–58,000 total — UNVERIFIED on living costs
scholarships: NL Scholarship €5,000 one-off, non-EEA only, by nomination not application. Excellence Scholarship for top entrance-exam performers (amount UNVERIFIED).
englishTest: 'In order to be admitted to a Bachelor's or Master's programme at the Royal Conservatoire, you need to have sufficient command of the English language.' Institution-wide standard is IELTS 6.0 / TOEFL 80 (as published for Sonology). Exact score for Art of Sound UNVERIFIED.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE (2026 intake): portfolio, Master Project Plan and CV due 26 February 2026; interview invitations notified 31 March 2026; motivation interviews week of 13 April 2026; final admission decision 31 August 2026. Expect the same rhythm for September 2027 — UNVERIFIED.
applicationOpens: After 1 December of the preceding year

institution: Royal Conservatoire The Hague (Institute of Sonology) with TU Berlin
program: Master specialisation in Audio Communication & Sonology
qualification: Master of Music in Sonology (Royal Conservatoire) / MSc Audio Communication and Technology (TU Berlin)
accreditationStatus: NVAO-accredited on the Dutch side; German accreditation on the TU Berlin side
language: English (TU Berlin component partly German — UNVERIFIED)
whatYouStudy: Combined scientific/engineering study of audio communication at TU Berlin with artistic electronic-music and sonology study at the Institute of Sonology.
entryRequirements: 'Bachelor's, master's, or graduate degree in science, engineering, humanities, social sciences, artistic-scientific, business, law, or equivalent'; 'good knowledge of English, good knowledge of higher mathematics (calculus, linear algebra)'; knowledge of a programming language or computer algebra system. For the Sonology track: background in composition, electronic/acoustic music, computer science, musicology, music perception, film studies, engineering, or performance.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — strongly. Engineering and computer-science bachelors are explicitly named, and higher mathematics plus programming are required. This is arguably the most non-music-friendly Field-A route in the region for a software-engineering graduate.
portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — not stated on the Royal Conservatoire page; primary application is to TU Berlin.
tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED — depends on which institution enrols the student. TU Berlin charges no tuition (semester contribution only, roughly €350/semester); Royal Conservatoire institutional fee is €11,488/yr. Must be confirmed.
englishTest: UNVERIFIED (no exact score published on the Royal Conservatoire page)
deadline: Applications go to TU Berlin, with the transfer option to The Hague, by 15 February of the year of entry. Restricted enrolment (numerus clausus). Start date October (not September).

institution: HKU University of the Arts Utrecht (Hogeschool voor de Kunsten Utrecht)
program: Master of Music, pathway Music Design (strands: Music Technology, Music Production, Sound Design, Composition)
institutionType: Public (government-funded university of applied sciences for the arts)
language: English (lessons taught in English; approximately two-thirds of students are Dutch)
whatYouStudy: Four strands which may be combined rather than chosen exclusively: Music Technology, Music Production, Sound Design, Composition. Self-directed artistic research around a personal project.
entryRequirements: Applicants must have 'completed a bachelor's degree in a relevant field or are active as a professional at a comparable level.' Submit motivation letter, study plan, CV and portfolio. 'No specific software proficiency is required for admission.' Cap of 25 students admitted each year.
acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — 'can make an exception for candidates without a Bachelor of Music, but only in case of exceptional talent and a steady track record.' Quoted verbatim. For a candidate with no portfolio yet this is a real obstacle; the exception is discretionary, not routine.
portfolioSpec: Motivation letter + study plan + CV + portfolio. Exact number of works, duration and format NOT specified on the programme page — UNVERIFIED.
auditionSpec: Selected candidates proceed to 'an online interview with the admissions committee.' No live audition.
tuitionNonEU: Institutional tuition fee — exact figure not published as a flat number; HKU directs applicants to its Tuition Fee Calculator. Statutory (EEA) fee 2026-2027 is €2,694. Non-EEA institutional master fee UNVERIFIED (comparable Dutch arts institutions charge €11,500–€13,000).
scholarships: NL Scholarship €5,000 one-off for non-EEA master's students. HKU Scholarship — amount and deadline UNVERIFIED.
englishTest: UNVERIFIED — programme page refers to the general enrolment requirements page without stating a score.
deadline: For 2026-2027 the application rounds were 24 November, 12 January, 16 February and 13 April. 'Non-EU/EEA applicants should apply by 1 April for visa processing.' PRIOR CYCLE — equivalent rounds expected for 2027-2028.
applicationOpens: Rounds open from November of the preceding year

institution: Codarts University of the Arts Rotterdam
program: Master of Music — Composition Profile / Performers Profile, available in the Pop, Jazz, Classical and World Music departments
institutionType: Public (government-funded university of applied sciences for the arts)
whatYouStudy: Self-directed master project as either a performing musician or a composer, in Classical, Jazz, Pop, Global Musics or a combination. Assessment by public concert (performers) or public composition presentation (composers). Students receive an annual budget of €500 toward their Master's goals.
entryRequirements: Demonstrated English fluency written and spoken; genre-specific audition material — Classical applicants prepare up to 5 contrasting pieces, other genres an approximately 30-minute programme showing stylistic diversity at bachelor-exam level.
acceptsNonMusic: NO / effectively no — admission is by audition at bachelor-graduation performance standard. UNVERIFIED whether a formal written exception exists, but the audition standard alone excludes a candidate with no music training.
portfolioSpec: Audition programme rather than a portfolio: approximately 30 minutes of music demonstrating stylistic diversity at the level of a bachelor's final exam (non-classical genres). Exact format UNVERIFIED from the official site (codarts.nl blocks automated retrieval; figures taken from the Mastersportal listing).
auditionSpec: Live/recorded audition required — this is a performance-entry conservatoire master, not a portfolio-entry one.
tuitionNonEU: €10,500 per year for non-EU/EEA students (per Mastersportal listing — NOT confirmed on codarts.nl, which blocks automated access. TREAT AS UNVERIFIED).
totalCostEstimate: ≈ €21,000 tuition over 2 years + living costs — UNVERIFIED
scholarships: NL Scholarship €5,000, merit-based, non-EU students, first year only.
englishTest: IELTS minimum 5.5 (per Mastersportal listing — UNVERIFIED against codarts.nl)
deadline: 8 April 2027 stated for the September 2027 intake (per Mastersportal — UNVERIFIED against codarts.nl). Start date 4 September 2027.

portfolioSpec: Application via Studielink plus passport copy and bachelor degree; an 'audition interview' follows. Exact portfolio spec UNVERIFIED.

deadline: PROGRAMME DISCONTINUED — 'This programme is being discontinued. From the 2025–2026 academic year onwards, no new students will be admitted.' NOT AVAILABLE for September 2027 entry.
